candidate.evidence: Old code returned `callback.__module__ + "." + callback.__qualname__` unless `__name__` was missing; new code calls `qualname(callback)` which raises ValueError when `"<" in value.__qualname__`, and the except branch returns `callback.__module__ + "." + callback.__class__.__name__`, i.e. "mod.function" for a locally defined view.
candidate.finding: lookup_str now falls back to the class-name form for any callback whose qualname contains '<' (e.g. views defined inside a function or decorator closure), where previously it returned the full `__qualname__`.
candidate.suggested_fix: Keep the `not hasattr(callback, '__name__')` check for the class-name fallback and only use qualname()'s ValueError path for genuinely unnamed callables, or return `module.__qualname__` for local functions.

candidate.evidence: `try: return qualname(view_func) except ValueError: return f"{view_func.__module__}.{view_func.__class__.__name__}"` — qualname raises ValueError for qualnames containing '<', so a closure-defined view falls into the class-name branch yielding "mod.function".
candidate.finding: get_view_name now reports "module.function" for view functions whose __qualname__ includes '<locals>' instead of the previous fully qualified name.
candidate.suggested_fix: Fall back to `view_func.__qualname__` when it exists and only use `__class__.__name__` when there is no __qualname__.

candidate.evidence: Removed `if self.value.__module__ is None: raise ValueError("Cannot serialize function %r: No module" % self.value)`; the new except branch formats the generic "Could not find function %s in %s." using `getattr(self.value, "__module__", None)`.
candidate.finding: The distinct error message for functions with no module is gone; a function with `__module__ is None` now produces "Could not find function X in None." instead of "Cannot serialize function %r: No module".
candidate.suggested_fix: Re-raise the module-specific message when `__module__` is None, or update tests/docs that assert on the old message.

candidate.evidence: `module = self.value.__self__.__module__` is used unconditionally for the returned imports set, while qualname() only validates the klass module inside its own branch; if it passed, fine, but the imports set is derived independently and not validated against the name returned.
candidate.finding: For bound classmethods the import statement may be built from a None module, producing "import None".
candidate.suggested_fix: Derive the module from the same source qualname() used, and assert it is non-empty before emitting `import %s`.

candidate.evidence: `return qualname(self.value), {"import %s" % module}` replaces `"%s.%s" % (module, self.value.__qualname__)`, and qualname raises ValueError when `"<" in value.__qualname__`.
candidate.finding: TypeSerializer now raises ValueError from qualname() for classes whose __qualname__ contains '<locals>' (or lacks __qualname__), where it previously returned a string; this changes migration serialization failures from a deconstruct-time string to an exception.
candidate.suggested_fix: Catch ValueError and raise the serializer's standard "Cannot serialize" error with a clear message, or keep the previous formatting for types.

candidate.evidence: The first branch returns `f"{module}.{klass.__qualname__}.{value.__name__}"` without checking `"<" in klass.__qualname__`, while the general path raises ValueError in that case.
candidate.finding: The bound-classmethod branch skips the '<' local-object check applied to other values, so a classmethod of a locally defined class returns a non-importable path like 'mod.outer.<locals>.C.meth' instead of raising ValueError.
candidate.suggested_fix: Apply the same `'<' in klass.__qualname__` validation in the __self__ branch.

candidate.evidence: The string branch produces `subelement_list = subelements.split('.')`; for `subelements=''` this yields `['']`, so `if not subelement_list:` is False and no AnsibleFilterError is raised despite the input being effectively empty.
candidate.finding: The new empty check does not cover the string form of `subelements`: an empty string is split into `['']`, which is truthy as a list, so the guard is bypassed and the filter proceeds to look up an empty key.
candidate.suggested_fix: Validate the raw input too, e.g. raise when `not subelements` (or filter out empty path components) before/in addition to checking `subelement_list`.

candidate.evidence: The new `raise AnsibleFilterError('subelements must not be empty')` executes before the `results` loop, whereas previously execution fell through to the iteration over `element_list`.
candidate.finding: Raising for an empty subelements list is a behavioural change that previously succeeded (returning each element paired with an empty/whole value); existing playbooks or tests passing `[]` will now fail hard.
candidate.suggested_fix: Document the new error in the filter docs/changelog and confirm no test asserts the old empty-list behaviour.

candidate.evidence: The TokenError branch now ends with `error_msg = (...)` and the following line `        errors[grammar.version] = InvalidInput(error_msg)` is at loop-body indentation rather than inside the `except TokenError` block.
candidate.finding: The `errors[grammar.version] = InvalidInput(error_msg)` assignment was de-indented out of the `except TokenError` handler into the `for` loop body, so it executes on every grammar iteration — including when parsing succeeds — and will raise `NameError`/`UnboundLocalError` when no exception set `error_msg`, or record a stale error from a previous grammar.
candidate.suggested_fix: Re-indent `errors[grammar.version] = InvalidInput(error_msg)` back inside the `except TokenError as te:` block.

candidate.evidence: `f"    {' ' * (column - 1)}^\n"` in both new error messages, with column taken directly from `err.context`/`te.args[1]`.
candidate.finding: `' ' * (column - 1)` assumes a 1-based column; if `column` is 0 (lib2to3/tokenize columns are frequently 0-based) the multiplication yields an empty string and the caret points at the wrong offset, one column left of the actual error.
candidate.suggested_fix: Confirm the column base and use `' ' * max(column, 0)` (or `column - 1` guarded by `max(..., 0)`) consistently.

candidate.evidence: Old: `f"Cannot parse{tv_str}: {lineno}:{column}: {faulty_line}"`; new adds newlines plus a literal `"SyntaxError: invalid syntax"`.
candidate.finding: The error message format changed from a single line to a multi-line block ending with a hardcoded "SyntaxError: invalid syntax"; existing tests and downstream consumers matching the old `Cannot parse...: {lineno}:{column}: {faulty_line}` string will break, and the hardcoded suffix can misdescribe non-syntax failures.
candidate.suggested_fix: Update affected tests/docs and derive the trailing message from the actual exception rather than hardcoding it.

candidate.evidence: `f"    {te.args[0]}\n" f"    {' ' * (column - 1)}^\n" "SyntaxError: invalid syntax"`, while the comment above notes these "typically don't have a 'faulty_line'".
candidate.finding: In the TokenError branch the second line printed is `te.args[0]` (the error text, e.g. "EOF in multi-line statement"), not source code, yet a caret line is rendered beneath it as if it were the faulty source line — producing a nonsensical pointer.
candidate.suggested_fix: Omit the caret line for TokenError, and use the actual token error message instead of the hardcoded "SyntaxError: invalid syntax" trailer.

gates.name: dataset certification
gates.target: all scored labels adjudicated and revision-valid

limitations: A label remains provisional until a named human records a final verdict and explicit approval; provisional labels force the dataset-certification gate to fail.

Finding-to-label matching is mechanical: same file, a line within 5, and at least 18% shared distinctive vocabulary. The eval plan asks for manual adjudication of ambiguous matches, which this run does not perform.
Label-overlap precision is a matching proxy, not adjudicated correctness. The report retains full findings so a human can assess unmatched output.
